introduction: 1 Kings records Solomon's succession and the securing of the throne, his wisdom and the ordering of the kingdom, the building and dedication of the temple, and his glory and fall; the division of the kingdom and the succession of kings in Judah and Israel; Elijah, the drought and Carmel, and Elijah at Horeb and the call of Elisha; and the Syrian wars, Naboth's vineyard, and Ramoth-gilead and the death of Ahab. These eleven studies follow literary divisions; they do not claim eleven independently dated historical events. Archaeology, historical reconstruction, and later interpretation are distinguished from biblical testimony.
